name: MA-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+11 district with a favorable national environment anchors Democratic fundamentals
Dan Koh out-raised Micah Jones roughly 10-to-1, with $1.8M in outside support and none opposed
Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee near 96%
Open seat with no polls or expert ratings, adding modest uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's eleven-point Democratic lean plus a favorable environment point to a comfortable hold, and Koh's overwhelming money advantage and near-96% market pricing reinforce that picture despite Moulton's retirement. No polls or expert ratings contradict the fundamentals.
model.watch: Late Republican outside spending or a sharp national shift toward the GOP could narrow what markets currently treat as a safe Democratic hold.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Seth Moulton (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Massachusetts' sixth district leans eleven points Democratic, and Seth Moulton's retirement to run for Senate creates an open seat rather than a competitive one. Dan Koh has raised $4.7 million to Micah Jones's $449,000, holds a large cash advantage, and benefits from $1.8 million in outside support with none opposing him. Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee at roughly 96 percent.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing. The national environment also favors Democrats this cycle. The seat stays in the Safe Democratic column, with the main uncertainty coming from the open-seat nature of the race rather than any sign of a genuine contest.
